Handoff: why Buddy workers ran on gpt-6-sol instead of gpt-6.1-sol
From: Wave Simulation Lead, at the owner's request in #iceblade (post_01a0eec5-ac81). Running workers were left untouched.

What happened
All 5 closeout workers run as codex / gpt-6-sol / high. That covers the ones I dispatched and the ones the CEO dispatched (runs run_01a0eeb5-bf5f, run_01a0eeb5-bf20, run_01a0eeb7-8c0f, run_01a0eeba-a66c).

How the model got picked
The model was never selected from the catalog. It was copied from prose.

The Buddy soul text pinned it. My soul (rev 8, the 2026-09-28 "cost-aware delegation" preference) said: "Codex GPT-6 Sol (gpt-6-sol) is the default execution model … Set the actual model to gpt-6-sol." The CEO's soul and memory, plus dispatch notes like wave_sim/agent_notes/2026-09-28_buddy_dispatch_memory_correction/, repeat the same literal id. Each dispatch copies the previous one.
The MCP post tool requires an exact id. In server/src/buddies/worker-config.ts, WorkerSchema.model is a required string. checkedRunConfig only checks that the id exists in the catalog. gpt-6-sol still exists there, so it passes.
Nothing auto-upgrades, by design. The code comment reads: "nothing falls back to the profile, so a worker never silently runs on a model nobody chose." An explicit, valid, older id is honored as written. There is also no "latest in family" alias for workers.
Where to see what's available
Humans: the config picker (client/src/views/config/config-options.ts). 1444cdd fixed a bug where the gpt-6- prefix match hid 6.1 Sol. That fix landed 2026-09-29 19:02Z, about 45 minutes before these workers launched. Before it, even the UI didn't show 6.1.
Buddies: no MCP tool lists the catalog. An agent only sees valid ids when it passes an invalid one and gets the error message back.
Source of truth: vendor/agent-cli-tool/catalog.jsonc and the generated copy at shared/src/generated/catalog.ts. The Codex provider's defaultModelId there is already gpt-6.1-sol. A worker that could say "provider default" would have gotten 6.1 automatically, but model is required.
Done now
My soul is updated (rev 9). The default is now "latest Sol in the live catalog (currently gpt-6.1-sol), never carry forward an old pinned id", and reasoningEffort must always be passed explicitly.
Why explicit effort matters: gpt-6.1-sol defaults to low effort, while gpt-6-sol defaulted to medium. Swapping only the model id without setting effort would quietly lower effort.
New dispatches from me will use gpt-6.1-sol. Running workers finish on 6-sol.
Recommended unleashd fixes (unowned; for whoever owns unleashd)
Worker model aliases. Accept model: "latest:sol" (or make model optional, meaning the provider defaultModelId). Resolve it once at dispatch and record the resolved id on the run. This keeps "no silent fallback", since the alias is an explicit, recorded choice, and ends id drift through prose.
Warn on superseded ids. When a worker names an id that has a newer family member (the same latestCodexModelIds logic the picker uses), return a warning in the post result, or refuse unless pin: true is set.
Expose the catalog to Buddies. Add a read-only providers/models MCP action listing ids, default model, default effort and levels.
Sweep souls and memories. Other Buddies (at least the CEO) still carry gpt-6-sol literals. Either do a one-time owner-approved edit, or rely on fix 2 to catch them.
Make runs readable. runs.get returns only metadata. To audit what workers were doing I had to read ~/.codex/sessions/.../rollout-*.jsonl directly. A runs.get transcript tail, or a pointer to the session file, would let leads verify workers through the MCP.
Claim boundary: this is a code and config read of ~/git/unleashd at acd7410. I did not verify the live server's loaded catalog beyond it accepting both ids.

## Follow-up: the ongoing Buddy DM grows without limit

**Status:** parked. Owner decision (2026-09-25): one ongoing DM per (workspace, Buddy) is fine for now. No work is scheduled.

**The problem:** a Buddy DM is a single conversation that resumes forever, and only deleting it starts a new one. Its native session keeps growing. Resumes get more expensive, and eventually the conversation hits the context window and falls back on the provider's auto-compaction.

**Proposal (not accepted, and nothing is built):**
- Keep one *visible* DM. Rotate the native session behind it with `resetProcess` in `server/src/conversations/runtime.ts` (DMs don't use it today) after about 6h idle or about 60% of the context window.
- The new session gets the briefing plus the last ~5 turns, with Wake tool calls stripped.
- Compaction stays as the fallback. An optional memory review can run before each reset.

**Check before building:** the 2026-09-12 audit (`agent_notes/2026-09-12-audit-history-cause.md`) found that `resetProcess` followed by a poll or restart *replaced* the visible history with the new native session. Later evidence points to `session-history-rotation.test.ts` for display retention. Confirm which one describes current behaviour first. If rotation still wipes the visible history, fix that before anything else.

**Pick up when:** DM resumes show up in `pnpm token-audit` as a top excess entry, or a DM reaches the context window.

## Thread follow-ups and thread seats: shipped, with follow-ups

**Shipped** on `feat/channels-project-view-2026-09-22`. Checked by tests and a live Claude gate smoke run. Not yet run end to end in the app:
- **Thread follow-ups** (`62b4fa2`): a new post in a thread asks each *other* Buddy who has posted there one yes/no question: "should you respond, or leave it to another team member?" Only a bare `<yes>` starts a reply. After 3 Buddy posts in a row, the thread waits for the owner.
- **Thread seats** (`1125dd0`, `9b0a6ca`): each Buddy has one conversation per thread, resumed for every reply there. The owner's harness/model pick on the @mention chip is saved on that conversation, and every later reply keeps it, including follow-ups and their yes/no question. Picking a different harness starts a new seat.
- **Why resuming is back:** 46b4c0c had switched to one conversation per mention because conversation 0f1dfb23 hit `out_of_tokens`. That was Codex's account usage limit, not the conversation growing too long.

## Channel navigation tools for agents: closed, with follow-ups

**Shipped** (pushed on `feat/channels-project-view-2026-09-22`, verified live):
- **@mention context:** the 10 latest posts, with each thread collapsed to a reply count and every line carrying its post id. In a thread, it's the first post plus the last 10 replies.
- `search_posts({query?, mentions: "me" | buddyId})` searches every channel, thread replies included.
- `get_thread({postId})` opens any post's thread. Given a reply, it opens centred on that reply. It pages with `before`/`after`.
- `get_list({listId, before|after|around})` starts from any post. Pages are anchored on post ids, so new posts can't shift a page. The old offset cursor and `threadId` options were deleted.
- Commits `4b9c09c`, `0f95fdc`, `66db722`, `aefa8bc`. Write-up: `agent_notes/20260924T113000Z_channel-agent-navigation-tools_product-development-lead_c51402b4.md`

**Follow-ups, open for pickup:**
1. **Bug:** `get_inbox({limit})` limits the channel list as well as messages. With `limit: 1` an agent sees one channel, and #triage-style discovery fails. The list of channels should not depend on the message limit.
2. **Unpushed package commits:** Buddies package commits `c844ac2` and `c4dfcdc` (`searchPosts`, `pagePosts`) live only in `~/git/.codex-worktrees/buddies/channel-agent-tools-20260924`, and that repo has no git remote. The code ships only in the vendored tarball. Needs a remote, or a merge into package `main`.
3. **Small bug, harmless:** paging `get_list`/`get_thread` with `before` from the oldest post returns an empty page with `newer: null`, even though the anchor post is newer. The caller already holds the anchor.
4. **Tool ideas, not started:**
   - A "threads with replies since my last read" filter, so a Wake catch-up doesn't scan every collapsed thread.
   - A channel directory an agent can read without going through the inbox.

**Editing tools: my recommendation is Remotion for the timeline and ffmpeg for everything else.**

- **ffmpeg alone** is fine for trimming, concatenating, cropping and encoding. It breaks down on exactly what this clip needs. Its `zoompan` filter is built for stills, so it jitters on moving video. A blur that eases in during scrolls means hand-writing timing expressions inside a filtergraph. And there's no preview, so every adjustment costs a full render.
- **Remotion** (React/TypeScript, renders in headless Chrome and then ffmpeg) turns the timeline into code:
  - clipping: `<Sequence>` plus video trim points
  - zoom: `interpolate()` with easing on a transform
  - blur: a blurred copy of the frame under a sharp, masked copy of the thread pane
  - cards and type: the same HTML/CSS as the beat 9 slides

  It fits our stack (pnpm, TypeScript), it can be re-rendered when the UI changes, and Remotion Studio gives you a scrubbable preview in the browser for reviewing drafts. Beat 9 already renders HTML frame-by-frame through our own headless-Chrome script. Remotion is that same idea, plus proper video-layer decoding, which we'd otherwise have to build ourselves.
- **Driving desktop software** (Final Cut, Resolve, Premiere through computer use) is slow and fragile, and it leaves nothing we can re-run. The useful middle ground: if you want to do fine timing by hand, I can export the cut as FCPXML and you open it in Final Cut. The code stays the source.
- **Also possible, not recommended:** Motion Canvas is great for animated explainers but weak with real footage. MLT/`melt` (Shotcut's engine) works, but its timelines are hand-written XML.

**One decision for you:** Remotion is free for individuals and companies of up to 3 people. Bigger teams need a paid company licence. If Unleashd is just you, it's free. I won't install anything until you say go.
